dedupe_keys.name: extreme weather and emergency management survey wxem of us emergency managers waves 1 10

description: The Extreme Weather and Emergency Management Survey series surveys emergency managers across the United States three to four times a year to understand emergency management operations, especially in relation to weather. Wave 1 opened on 4 August 2022 and recruited 720 emergency management personnel from a database of emergency managers built by the Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis at the University of Oklahoma, collecting location, jurisdiction type and experience. Later waves cover varied operational topics; wave 10, designed with collaborators at the National Severe Storms Laboratory and opened on 29 April 2026, asked 218 respondents about their use and understanding of National Weather Service flood products and perceived flood risk. Each wave on Harvard Dataverse provides the survey data as a tab-separated file, the questionnaire and a reference report with methodology and response frequencies, and is freely downloadable under CC0 1.0. Caveats: respondents come from IPPRA's database of emergency managers, response numbers vary by wave, and topics change between waves. It is useful for representing emergency manager decisions in emergency response and agent-based warning models and for studying how forecasts support resilience; a related record is the CHIME agent-based model of hurricane evacuation.
name: Extreme Weather and Emergency Management Survey (WxEM) of US emergency managers, waves 1-10
notes: One record covers waves 1 to 10 (ten Harvard Dataverse datasets). Reference: Wanless, A. et al. WxEM Wave 1. Harvard Dataverse. doi:10.7910/DVN/8VUUDA
provider: Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis (IPPRA), University of Oklahoma
